helpful: fedcourts query --include-applications surfaced recent resolved substantive applications whose escalation-signal columns made the no-signal-then-denied pattern easy to verify

CourtListener docket search established the applicant's pro se litigation history cheaply
gaps: No way to filter corpus application priors by applicant representation status or respondent type (court-as-respondent vs. adverse party), which is the strongest signal on this cell
The snapshot carries no last-polled timestamp visible to the cell, so judging staleness requires inference from the disposition-timing pattern rather than a recorded fact
The interim section publishes no time-to-disposition distribution; one would sharpen both staleness detection and the unscored timing forecast
notes: Interim arrival cell with no published baseline (strictly-prior pool 47 < 50 floor); anchored on the record and corpus priors alone.
